ownerSelectedScope: Familiar Georgian words from any subject; not restricted to strictly everyday use. Existing 3–6-letter and all other vocabulary rules remain.
method: Exact-spelling deduplication against all content JSON and all VOCABULARY review JSON/text, including approved, rejected, skipped, unselected and pending spellings. Individually read primary explanatory-dictionary definitions, bilingual dictionary entries and linked specialist/cultural sources. Rejected dictionary search-result pages as evidence of a definition; replaced ambiguous spellings and unsupported senses. Cached definitions were re-read, with available source hashes retained.
limitations: The exact 19 selected senses are owner-approved and await integration. The other 70 remain unapproved for required use, without an explicit all-gameplay exclusion. Eleven previously removed entries remain review history. Do not propose any of the original 100 spellings again as new.

Removed all six ordinals, both approximate-colour adjectives and three analogous prefixed adjectives. The latter three are explicitly recorded as an editorial application, not individually quoted owner rejections.
Familiarity is an editorial proposal across broad subjects, not a claim that every Georgian speaker knows every remaining word. No native-speaker review is claimed.
Previous individual exclusions, plural/grammar/name/barbarism rules and the 3–6-letter limit remain. მეორე was not in the original 100 and remains excluded by its earlier decision.
Batch 16 remains pending in full. Total approvals are 2,358, including 52 awaiting integration from batches 13–15 and 17. Active revision 30 stays at 2,306 required approvals and 500 levels.
No gameplay files, board fit, campaign capacity or repetition change was applied or measured. დარტსი has primary usage evidence rather than a standalone dictionary definition.
sourceAttribution: Short adapted English glosses only. Sources: Georgian Explanatory Dictionary / Linguistic Technologies Group; TSU English–Georgian Dictionary; NPLG hosted dictionaries and published references; University of Georgia synonym dictionary; CSS social-science dictionary; Japanese Embassy in Georgia; a primary Georgian product description. Full definitions are not reproduced.
